checks.finding: The ## Problem Evidence section describes an incident 'Observed on 2026-09-03 during epic-193-a5-capability-resolver spec attempt 14 (post-Done provenance re-bind)' citing 'reviewer A, seq0877, CONSTRAINTS-EXPLICIT', 'seq0879/0880', and 'spec-review-precheck.sh line 333'. None of these are rows in the supplied retrospective (reports/retrospective/2026-08-14T034801Z-pillar-a-wave-session.md) or RT-IDs under docs/review-tickets/. That retrospective explicitly states: 'Three of the six features (epic-192, epic-196, and eight of epic-193's ten tasks) are still Planned and contribute no measurements at all' (line 20-21), and its Review Gate Metrics table lists `epic-193`, `epic-194`, `epic-196` as 'N/A' / '—' across every column. The retrospective is dated 2026-08-14T034801Z, three weeks before the WFI's cited incident date of 2026-09-03, so no row in it can cover this incident by construction. No RT-ID is cited and no docs/review-tickets/ file exists for late August/September 2026 (latest on disk is RT-20260826-002.yml).

WFI-062.md contains no '## Root Cause Hypothesis' heading at all. The document's section order is '## Problem Evidence' -> '## Why-Why Chain' -> '## Proposed Change', with no standalone root-cause statement to evaluate for plausibility or for alignment with the Why-Why chain's terminal Because.

Multiple defects. (1) Format: the section is titled '## Why-Why Chain' rather than '## Why-Why Analysis', uses unnumbered inline Q&A bullets rather than numbered why-levels, and has no Evidence column. (2) Evidenced: none of the 4 levels cites a retrospective row, RT-ID, BL-ID, report path, or file:line, and none is marked '(hypothesis)' -- quoting each: L1 'Why did round 2 refuse to start? Because the precheck's changed-inputs predicate compares only requirements_sha256 and acceptance_sha256 against the prior round's contract.'; L2 'Why does it compare only those two? Because the state machine models "human edits between rounds" as edits to the two review-subject documents, the shape every pre-amendment attempt had.'; L3 'Why is that model now wrong? Because the Amendment Re-Review Context mechanism ... made investigation.md a first-class review subject ...'; L4 'Why was this not caught earlier? Every prior amendment attempt happened to edit requirements.md/acceptance-tests.md in the same round-fix, masking the gap ...'. 4 of 4 levels (100%, >= half) are unevidenced, which is Major under rule 6. (3) Terminates at mechanism: the chain's actual final Because (L4) is a circumstantial explanation of why the defect went undetected ('attempt 14 was the first whose sole defect lay in the amendment record itself'), not a controllable process/mechanism cause -- the real mechanism statement sits at L3's Because, but the chain does not terminate there. (4) Chained: L4's Why ('was this not caught earlier?') does not follow from L3's Because (about investigation.md becoming a first-class review subject) -- it silently changes subject from 'why is the model wrong' to 'why wasn't this detected sooner', breaking the required Why-of-prior-Because linkage.

Category is plugin-improvement. The '## Proposed Change' section (not the exempted Problem Evidence section) contains the forbidden term 'sdd-review-loop' (the plugin's own name): 'In `plugins/sdd-review-loop/scripts/spec-review-precheck.sh` (and the `.ps1` twin), extend the round>1 changed-inputs predicate to include `investigation.md` ...'. Per wfi-category-guide.md Section 2, `sdd-review-loop (plugin name)` must be substituted with `review gate plugin`.

The Proposed Change row/paragraph names a Target File inside `plugins/`: 'In `plugins/sdd-review-loop/scripts/spec-review-precheck.sh` (and the `.ps1` twin) ...'. Per the shared rule with NO-PLUGIN-SCOPE-CREEP, a `plugins/` path is a Major finding regardless of description unless the carve-out applies; as detailed under NO-PLUGIN-SCOPE-CREEP below, the carve-out does not apply here (condition 2 fails), so this row fails CHANGE-CONCRETE even though its Change Description text is otherwise concrete and non-vague.

## Expected Effect names no generic metric from wfi-category-guide.md Section 2 (e.g., 'average specification review gate round count', 'specification review gate blocked rate') and states no quantitative baseline-to-target change. Quote: 'A finding whose cure is an investigation.md edit becomes fixable in the next round like any other finding, measured by: re-running the attempt-14 round-2 transition with ONLY the investigation.md pin-fix applied (no requirements.md edit) exits 0 instead of failing with "reviewed inputs are unchanged from the prior round".' This is a pass/fail regression-test description, not a named metric with a numeric target.

No '## Verification Metric' section exists anywhere in WFI-062.md. Only '## Verification Plan' is present, and it is a code-fixture test plan (regression fixture, counter-fixture, mutation check, calibration-tests-untouched check), not a section naming one primary metric with baseline, target, and next checkpoint.

The '## Verification Plan' does not reference any specific retrospective metric row from reports/retrospective/2026-08-14T034801Z-pillar-a-wave-session.md. It cites 'a spec-review attempt directory whose round-1 contract is NEEDS_WORK', a 'counter-fixture', and 'review-prompt-calibration.tests.sh untouched' -- none of which are retrospective metric rows, consistent with the fact that Problem Evidence itself is not sourced from that retrospective either.

Target File `plugins/sdd-review-loop/scripts/spec-review-precheck.sh` (and `.ps1` twin) is inside `plugins/`: 'In `plugins/sdd-review-loop/scripts/spec-review-precheck.sh` (and the `.ps1` twin), extend the round>1 changed-inputs predicate to include `investigation.md` ...'. Carve-out assessed: (1) Category: plugin-improvement -- holds. (2) The `## Category` section must state, in its own words, that this repository is the plugin's source of truth and the change travels as a repository commit -- FAILS: the `## Category` section in WFI-062.md contains only the literal field line 'Category: plugin-improvement' with no such statement. (3) `## GitHub-Issue` section is present but contains only the boilerplate placeholder 'GitHub-Issue: PENDING — to be created by wfi-audit-cycle', not an issue URL, and this placeholder is used regardless of source-of-truth status so it cannot substitute for condition 2. Because condition 2 fails, the carve-out does not apply, and this Major finding stands unconditionally.

proposed_revisions.change: Either hold this WFI until an updated retrospective actually measures epic-193-a5-capability-resolver spec review activity and cite the specific row/RT-ID it produces, or explicitly recharacterize the evidence as a live incident report awaiting retrospective capture and route it accordingly rather than presenting it as retrospective-backed friction.
proposed_revisions.rationale: Resolves EVIDENCE-CITED: the current retrospective (2026-08-14) predates the cited 2026-09-03 incident and explicitly excludes epic-193 from measurement this period, so no traceable citation currently exists.

proposed_revisions.change: Add a '## Root Cause Hypothesis' section immediately after Problem Evidence, e.g.: 'The round>1 changed-inputs predicate compares only requirements_sha256 and acceptance_sha256 because it was written before investigation.md became a first-class review subject under the Amendment Re-Review Context mechanism; a finding curable only by an investigation.md edit therefore has no lawful transition path.' Ensure this is the exact terminal mechanism the Why-Why chain reaches.
proposed_revisions.rationale: ROOT-CAUSE-PLAUSIBLE requires this section and it is currently entirely absent.

proposed_revisions.change: Rename to '## Why-Why Analysis', convert to numbered Why/Because levels with an Evidence column (citing spec-review-precheck.sh:333/344, seq IDs, or explicit '(hypothesis)' markers on each row), and either remove the 'why wasn't this caught earlier' aside or make it visibly subordinate so the chain terminates at the mechanism already identified at the current Level 3 (investigation.md not modeled as a review subject) rather than at the circumstantial 'attempt 14 was the first...' explanation.
proposed_revisions.rationale: Resolves the WHY-CHAIN-VALID Major finding: current chain is unevidenced on all 4 levels and terminates on a non-mechanism, circumstantial cause with a subject break at Level 4.

proposed_revisions.change: Remove the literal plugin path and the plugin name 'sdd-review-loop'; describe the change generically per wfi-category-guide.md Section 2 (e.g., 'the review gate plugin's specification review round-transition check') and state that delivery is via a GitHub Issue against the plugin per the plugin-improvement routing lane -- OR, if this repository is genuinely the plugin's own source-of-truth repo, add an explicit statement to that effect in '## Category' and a real issue URL / filing-timing statement in '## GitHub-Issue' to satisfy the carve-out before naming the plugins/ path directly.
proposed_revisions.rationale: Resolves the Critical CATEGORY-LANGUAGE-MATCH finding (forbidden term 'sdd-review-loop'), the CHANGE-CONCRETE Major finding, and the NO-PLUGIN-SCOPE-CREEP Major finding together, since all three point at the same row.

proposed_revisions.change: State the improvement using a Section 2 generic metric name plus a quantitative baseline-to-target change, e.g. 'Reduce the count of specification review gate attempts with no lawful round-2 transition from N (baseline once measured) to 0 over the next 3 amendment-triggered spec review attempts,' in addition to the existing pass/fail regression description.
proposed_revisions.rationale: EFFECT-MEASURABLE requires a named generic metric and a numeric target; the current text only describes a binary test-exit-code outcome.

proposed_revisions.change: Add a '## Verification Metric' section naming exactly one primary metric (e.g., 'spec-review attempts blocked by an unreachable round transition, count'), its current baseline (or an explicit '0 measured to date' if genuinely untracked), a quantitative target (e.g., '0'), and a next checkpoint (e.g., 'after the next 3 amendment-triggered spec-review attempts').
proposed_revisions.rationale: VERIFICATION-METRIC-DEFINED requires this section; it is currently missing entirely from WFI-062.md.

proposed_revisions.change: Add a line naming which specific retrospective Review Gate Metrics row(s) (e.g., Spec Review Rounds / Spec Review Verdict for the affected feature) will be compared in the next retrospective cycle, alongside the existing fixture/mutation checks.
proposed_revisions.rationale: VERIFICATION-PLAN-SPECIFIC (Minor): the current plan cites only code fixtures, never a retrospective metric row to be compared next cycle.
